children.text:
By dealing with tasks sequentially, not concurrently.

I feel that now we can spin up agents to tackle multiple projects or tasks at once, we end up context switching more than ever before, which seems like a fast track to burnout.

source.text:
I wonder if anyone else is experiencing the specific type of burnout that comes from working with AI tools. I think there are a couple of reasons that it is different from regular workload burnout.

1. It feels that we are more divorced or removed from the day-to-day work and we have less understanding of what we're doing. 2. I see that there's not that same sense of accomplishment of building something. 3. The volume and the tools that we have to review the changes seem to be inadequate to handle the amount of code and the amount of changes that are happening.

I can see it on my teams, how they're dealing with it and trying to come up with a workflow. I can see it on myself as I'm trying to work on my side projects, and it just feels like I'm slowly burning out deeper than before.
source.title: Ask HN: How are you dealing with AI burnout?
